title: Catena-X Battery Pass aspect model
usedFor: Candidate semanticId for the battery submodel template in the AAS projection.
licence: CC-BY-4.0. Confirmed 2026-08-11 directly from the model file's own SPDX header (`github.com/eclipse-tractusx/sldt-semantic-models`), matching what was already recorded — copyright held jointly by BASF, BMW, CGI Deutschland, Henkel, Robert Bosch, SAP, T-Systems, ZF Friedrichshafen and Eclipse Foundation contributors.
finding: Field-by-field comparison against `BatteryData` (`crates/dpp-domain/src/domain/sector/data/battery.rs`) done 2026-08-11. Core identity/performance fields correspond closely (battery category, chemistry, rated capacity/energy/voltage, min/max voltage, cycle counts, the Annex VII state-of-health parameter set, resistance and fade rates). The gaps found here **independently corroborate** the same gaps found comparing `batterypass-samm` the same day — this is now two unrelated organisations' models agreeing on what our own model is missing, which is stronger evidence than either alone: hazardous-substance declarations (`hazardousCadmium`, `hazardousMercury`, `hazardousSubstance`, `impactOfSubstances` — nothing analogous to the `SvhcSubstance` list electronics and textile both carry), a `warranty` field (we have none), conformity/labelling (`declarationOfConformity`, `declarationOfConformityId`, `meaningOfLabels`, `testReport`), and end-of-life/safety (`separateCollection`, `wastePrevention`, `safeDischarging`, `removalFromAppliance`, `dismantling`, `fireClass`, `usableExtinguishAgent`, `safety`, `safetyMeasures`). Broader than `batterypass-samm`: also carries `dueDiligencePolicy`, `euTaxonomyDisclosureStatement` and `sustainabilityReport` — ESG-disclosure fields with no correspondence in `BatteryData` at all. This is the identifier `dpp-aas`'s battery submodel already treats as a candidate `semanticId` (see `crates/dpp-aas/src/sectors/battery.rs`) but the correspondence check this record's own `nextStep` asked for had never been done before now.
nextStep: Same caveat as `batterypass-samm`: the gaps above are candidates, not adoptable fields — each needs its own Battery Regulation citation (Annex VI/VII/XIII or an article) before becoming an `Option` on `BatteryData`, this vocabulary having the field is not a legal basis. Where `dpp-aas` already emits `urn:samm:io.catenax.battery.battery_pass` as a semanticId, confirm that usage sits behind the same `BridgeNotSpeakable` gate as every other conformance-bridge entry — verified status here changes what we may compare against, not what we may emit.
